correctness.rationale: The shortest nonwrapping spans containing two and three ones give the cut predicate a≤b,c; zero-start cuts fail at length one. A qualifying nonminimum gap forces every smaller gap to be its predecessor. Hence with several minimum gaps only minima qualify; with a unique minimum a rotated first there is exactly one possible extra cut, before b, qualifying if b≤c,d. Subtracting a leaves three positive gaps; their unrestricted series is z³/(1−z)³ and the extra-cut subcase has series z³/((1−z³)(1−z)²). Multiplying the difference by z⁴/(1−z⁴) gives N_1. Exactly three minimum gaps and all equal gaps give N_3 and N_4 directly; Burnside gives the total, including half-turn and quarter-turn ties, and N_2 follows by subtraction. Pole orders yield the stated asymptotics. A fresh exhaustive weak-order polynomial check reproduced the four numerators, and direct literal tests of all physical cuts of all four-one necklaces for lengths 4–32 agreed, including (111,129,4,1) at length 20.
residual_risks: Finite replay is corroboration; the structural count gives all lengths. Periodic equality of cut words must not be used to identify physical cuts.

value.rationale: Valid rotation counts measure the non-uniqueness of linear prefix-normal representatives obtainable by cutting without editing a circle. Four ones is a natural fixed-composition family, with a genuine difference between ordinary and periodic comparisons. A complete distribution, including tied and periodic configurations and the asymptotic two-class law, is a useful exact baseline rather than an arbitrary length cutoff.
